verse.text: And they said one to the other: Was not our heart burning within us, whilst he spoke in the way, and opened to us the scriptures?

bible.intro: The road to Emmaus. Read it slowly, and picture yourself as the third person walking with the two disciples.
questions: What were the two disciples feeling as they walked? When have you felt the same way?
Jesus walked with them before they recognized him. Where might he have been walking with you without your noticing?
They recognized him "in the breaking of the bread." What do you think that phrase points to?

discuss: What first made you curious about the Catholic faith?
What is one question you hope to have answered this year?
Who has walked beside you on your spiritual journey so far?

quiz.q: About how far was Emmaus from Jerusalem?
quiz.why: Luke says the village was about seven miles from Jerusalem (Luke 24:13).

quiz.q: When did the disciples recognize Jesus?
quiz.why: Their eyes were opened at the table, when he took bread, blessed it and broke it (Luke 24:30-31).

quiz.q: What do you need before starting this journey?
options: Nothing but an open heart and your questions
quiz.why: The disciples were full of doubts too. Questions are welcome; that is what this time is for.

verse.text: Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.

bible.intro: Jesus teaches about prayer and gives us the Our Father.
questions: Jesus says to pray in your "inner room." Where could your quiet place be this week?
Which line of the Our Father speaks to you most right now? Why?
Jesus links our forgiveness with forgiving others. Is there someone you find it hard to forgive?

discuss: How did you pray as a child, if at all? How do you pray now?
What makes prayer hard for you: time, distraction, not knowing what to say?
What is one small prayer habit you could try this week?

quiz.q: What is prayer, at its simplest?
options: Lifting your heart and mind to God
quiz.why: Prayer is lifting the heart and mind to God (Catechism 2559). No special words are needed.

quiz.q: Which prayer did Jesus himself teach his disciples?
quiz.why: When the disciples asked "Lord, teach us to pray," he gave them the Our Father (Luke 11:1-4).

quiz.q: Which of these is a good simple daily habit?
options: Offering your day to God when you wake up
quiz.why: Start the day with the Sign of the Cross and an offering, and end it by thanking God for one good thing.

verse.text: And we have known, and have believed the charity, which God hath to us. God is charity: and he that abideth in charity, abideth in God, and God in him.
verse.note: "Charity" is the old English word for love.

bible.intro: Jesus sends the apostles to baptize "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit."
questions: Notice it says "in the name" (one name), not "names." What does that hint about the Trinity?
Some of the disciples "doubted" even as they worshiped. What do you make of that?
Jesus promises "I am with you always." Where do you need to hear that this week?

discuss: How would you explain the Trinity to a friend in one or two sentences?
Faith is both believing and trusting. Which comes easier to you?
What does "God is love" mean to you personally?

quiz.q: How many Persons are in the one God?
quiz.why: One God in three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Catechism 253).

quiz.q: Is the Father the same Person as the Son?
options: No, but each is fully God
quiz.why: Each Person is fully God, and each is distinct from the others (Catechism 253-254).

quiz.q: Faith involves...
options: The mind believing and the will trusting
quiz.why: Faith is the intellect believing what God reveals and the will entrusting ourselves to him (Catechism 150, 155).

quiz.q: What does 1 John 4:16 say God is?
quiz.why: "God is love" (1 John 4:8, 16).

verse.text: God, who, at sundry times and in divers manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son.

bible.intro: The lost sheep and the lost coin: a God who goes looking for us.
questions: The shepherd leaves ninety-nine to find one. What does that say about how God sees you?
Have you ever felt lost, or been found? What was it like?
Heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents. How does that change how you see confession?

discuss: Has there been a moment when you felt God was reaching out to you?
Why do you think God reveals himself step by step instead of all at once?
Scripture, Tradition and the Magisterium: which of these was new to you?

quiz.q: Divine Revelation is...
options: Humans figuring out God on their own
God making himself and his plan known to us
A new book written every century
quiz.why: Revelation is God freely making himself known (Catechism 50-51).

quiz.q: How is God's Word handed on in the Church?
options: Scripture and Tradition, guarded by the Magisterium
quiz.why: Like a three-legged stool: Scripture, Tradition and the Magisterium work together (Catechism 95).

quiz.q: What is the Magisterium?
options: The teaching office of the Pope and bishops
quiz.why: The Magisterium is the living teaching office of the Church (Catechism 85).

quiz.q: Is there new public revelation after Jesus?
options: No, in Jesus God has said everything
quiz.why: In his Son, God has spoken his full and final Word (Catechism 65-66).

verse.text: Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths.
verse.note: Psalm 119:105 in newer Bibles; the old Latin-based numbering is one behind for most psalms.

bible.intro: Paul tells Timothy what Scripture is for.
questions: Paul says Scripture is "inspired by God." What does inspired mean to you after this lesson?
Who taught you the faith "from infancy," or who is teaching you now?
Which of the four uses (teaching, correcting, training, equipping) do you need most?

discuss: Do you own a Bible? Which translation, and how do you find reading it?
Which book of the Bible would you like to read first, and why?
Why do you think the Church reads the Bible with Tradition, not alone?

quiz.q: How many books are in the Catholic Bible?
quiz.why: 46 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New Testament. Most Protestant Bibles have 66.

quiz.q: Who is the author of Scripture?
options: God, working through real human authors
quiz.why: God inspired human writers who used their own words and skills (Catechism 105-106).

quiz.q: Catholics read the Bible...
options: Paying attention to what each author meant and the kind of writing it is
quiz.why: We read it literarily, with attention to history, culture and literary form (Catechism 109-110).

quiz.q: A covenant is...
options: A sacred family bond sealed with an oath
quiz.why: Contracts exchange property; covenants exchange persons and make us family.

verse.text: For God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son; that whosoever believeth in him, may not perish, but may have life everlasting.

bible.intro: The fall, and the first promise of a Savior.
questions: How does the serpent twist God's words? Where do you hear similar lies today?
After they sin, Adam and Eve hide and blame. How do you see that pattern in yourself?
Verse 15 is called the "first Gospel." What promise does God make even here?

discuss: Where do you see the "broken lines" between people in the world today?
Why do you think God gave us freedom, knowing we could misuse it?
What does it mean to you that the Church is God's family?

quiz.q: What are the three parts of the story of salvation?
quiz.why: Creation, Fall and Redemption: the shape of the whole Bible.

quiz.q: Original sin is...
options: A wounded human nature we inherit
quiz.why: We are born without the holiness and friendship with God we were made for (Catechism 404-405).

quiz.q: Which promise to Abraham is fulfilled in Jesus?
quiz.why: Jesus opens God's family to the whole world in the new covenant.

quiz.q: "Catholic" means...
quiz.why: From the Greek for "according to the whole" (Catechism 830-831).

verse.text: Jesus saith to him: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me.

bible.intro: "Who do you say that I am?"
questions: Jesus first asks what others say, then what you say. Why both?
Peter gets the answer right, but not from his own cleverness. Where did it come from?
How would you answer Jesus' question today, in your own words?

discuss: Who did you think Jesus was before you started RCIA? Has that changed?
Why does it matter that Jesus is both truly God and truly man?
What is one way you could get to know Jesus personally this week?

quiz.q: Jesus is...
quiz.why: One divine Person with two natures (Catechism 464, 469).

quiz.q: Which heresy said the Son was a creature, not God?
quiz.why: The Council of Nicaea (325) answered Arius: "begotten, not made."

quiz.q: Why is Mary called Theotokos, Mother of God?
options: Her Son is one divine Person
quiz.why: Ephesus (431) taught this to protect the truth about who Jesus is (Catechism 466).

quiz.q: Docetism taught that Jesus...
options: Only seemed to have a body
quiz.why: From the Greek dokein, "to seem."

verse.text: Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

bible.intro: The crucifixion of Jesus.
questions: Who stands at the foot of the cross? Where would you have been?
Jesus gives Mary to John, and John to Mary. What might that mean for you?
"It is finished." What did Jesus finish?

discuss: What do you usually do when you suffer? What would "offering it up" look like?
Why do you think the cross became the main sign of Christianity?
What does the Resurrection change about how you see death?

quiz.q: "Paschal" comes from the word for...
quiz.why: Jesus is the new Passover Lamb (1 Corinthians 5:7).

quiz.q: Why could Jesus bridge the gap of sin?
options: He was a very good man
He is both God and man
quiz.why: As man he could stand in our place; as God his offering had infinite worth.

quiz.q: "He descended into hell" in the Creed means...
options: The realm of the dead, to free the just
quiz.why: Sheol or Hades, the realm of the dead (Catechism 632-637).

quiz.q: We share in Christ's cross by...
options: Uniting our work, joys and sufferings with his
quiz.why: Catechism 618.

verse.text: And hope confoundeth not: because the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us.

bible.intro: Pentecost: the Holy Spirit comes on the Church.
questions: What signs show the Spirit's coming? What might each mean?
The crowd hears in their own languages. What does that say about the Church?
Where do you need the Spirit's courage this week?

discuss: When have you felt a nudge or strength that you couldn't explain?
Which gift of the Spirit do you most want: wisdom, courage, understanding?
What does "grace" mean to you so far?

verse.text: And I say to thee: That thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

bible.intro: The life of the first Christian community.
questions: List the four things the first Christians "devoted themselves" to. Which do you already share?
What would it look like for your parish to be like this?
Why do you think people were drawn to them?

discuss: Have you ever thought you could follow Jesus without the Church? What changed?
What has helped you feel at home in your parish, or what would?
Why do you think Jesus built a Church instead of leaving only a book?

verse.text: And Mary said: My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.

bible.intro: The Annunciation: Mary's yes.
questions: Mary asks a question but still says yes. What is the difference between her question and doubt?
What is God asking you to say yes to right now?
How does Mary's yes help you see her role in the Church?

discuss: What did you think about Mary before RCIA?
Do you have a favorite saint, or one you'd like to know?
How is asking a saint to pray for you like asking a friend?

verse.text: Jesus said to her: I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live:

bible.intro: Jesus raises Lazarus.
questions: Martha is honest about her disappointment. Can you be that honest with Jesus?
"Jesus wept." What does that tell you about how he sees your grief?
What would you like to say to Jesus about death and eternal life?

discuss: How do you feel when you think about death?
What do you imagine heaven is like? What does the Church say?
Why do Catholics pray for those who have died?

verse.text: Jesus answered: Amen, amen I say to thee, unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

bible.intro: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night.
questions: Nicodemus comes "at night." Why might he have come then?
What do you think "born of water and Spirit" means?
How is Baptism a new birth?

discuss: If you are already baptized, what do you know about your baptism? If not, what do you hope for?
What does it mean to be sealed with the Holy Spirit in Confirmation?
Who could be your sponsor or godparent, and why?

verse.text: I am the living bread which came down from heaven. If any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever; and the bread that I will give, is my flesh, for the life of the world.

bible.intro: The Bread of Life discourse.
questions: What does Jesus mean by "I am the bread of life"?
Many walk away when the teaching is hard. Why does Peter stay?
What do you hunger for that only God can fill?

discuss: What do you understand about the Real Presence so far?
Why do you think Jesus chose bread and wine?
How can you prepare to receive Communion for the first time?

verse.text: And taking bread, he gave thanks, and brake; and gave to them, saying: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this for a commemoration of me.

bible.intro: The Last Supper.
questions: Jesus says "do this in memory of me." What is the "this"?
Which part of the Mass do you understand least so far?
How could you prepare differently for Mass this Sunday?

discuss: What surprised you most the first time you went to Mass?
Which part of the Mass are you starting to love?
Why do you think the Mass follows the same pattern everywhere in the world?

verse.text: Receive ye the Holy Ghost. Whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them; and whose sins you shall retain, they are retained.

bible.intro: The prodigal son and the merciful father.
questions: Which son do you relate to more, and why?
The father runs to meet his son. What does that say about confession?
What does the older brother need to hear?

discuss: What feelings come up when you think about confession?
Why do you think Jesus gave us a sacrament for forgiveness instead of only private prayer?
Who in your life needs the comfort of the Anointing of the Sick?

verse.text: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

bible.intro: The wedding at Cana.
questions: Why might Jesus have chosen a wedding for his first sign?
Mary says "Do whatever he tells you." How could you live that this week?
Water becomes wine. Where do you need God to transform something ordinary?

discuss: What marriages have inspired you, and why?
Why do you think marriage and priesthood are called sacraments "at the service of communion"?
How could you pray for the priests and married couples in your parish?

verse.text: If you love me, keep my commandments.

bible.intro: The Beatitudes.
questions: Which Beatitude surprises you most?
Which one describes someone you admire?
Which one would you like to grow in?

discuss: Is it freeing or hard to think of commandments as a way of love?
Where do you see the difference between freedom to do anything and freedom to do good?
What helps you choose the good when it's hard?

verse.text: Charity is patient, is kind: charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely; is not puffed up;

bible.intro: Paul's hymn to love.
questions: Replace "love" with your own name. Which lines feel true, and which don't yet?
Why does Paul say that without love, even great gifts are nothing?
Which quality of love would you like to grow in this week?

discuss: Where did you learn what love is?
How is real love different from how love is shown in movies?
Who in your life loves in the way Paul describes?

verse.text: Or know you not, that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost, who is in you, whom you have from God; and you are not your own?

bible.intro: Man and woman made for each other.
questions: What does "it is not good for the man to be alone" tell us about people?
Why do you think the body matters to God?
How does seeing your body as a temple change how you treat it?

discuss: What messages about the body and sex did you grow up with?
What part of the Church's teaching here is new or hard for you?
How can we speak about this with kindness and truth?

verse.text: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.

bible.intro: The judgment of the nations.
questions: Which of the six works of mercy is easiest for you? Which is hardest?
Both groups are surprised. Why?
Who are "the least" in your town?

discuss: Where do you see Jesus in people who are struggling?
What is one need in your community your parish could help with?
How can small acts of mercy change a neighborhood?

verse.text: And God created man to his own image: to the image of God he created him. Male and female he created them.

bible.intro: Made in God's image.
questions: What does it mean to be made "in God's image"?
God calls creation "very good." Do you believe that about yourself?
Whose dignity is easy to forget in our world?

discuss: Have you ever been treated as less than you are? How did it feel?
Where do you see human dignity ignored today?
What would change if we saw every person as God's image?

verse.text: Now therefore saith the Lord: Be converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts, and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God.

bible.intro: Jesus on almsgiving, prayer and fasting.
questions: Why does Jesus stress doing these things in secret?
Which of the three is hardest for you?
What could you give up, and what could you add, this Lent?

discuss: What have your Lents looked like before, if any?
What is one habit you want to break, and one you want to build?
How can your class support each other through Lent?

verse.text: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

bible.intro: The man born blind.
questions: The man's sight comes in stages. How has your faith grown in stages?
Who in the story is really blind?
Where do you need Jesus to open your eyes?

discuss: What does it mean to "turn toward Christ"?
What would you like Jesus to heal in you before Easter?
How can we pray for each other during the scrutinies?

verse.text: For if thou confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in thy heart that God hath raised him up from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

bible.intro: The heart of what we believe.
questions: Paul lists what he "handed on." What is at the center?
Why does Paul list witnesses?
Which line of the Creed means most to you now?

discuss: Which part of the Creed was hardest for you to believe at first?
What does it mean that the Creed is "handed on" to you?
How would you say the Creed in your own words?

verse.text: Thus therefore shall you pray: Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.

bible.intro: Jesus teaches us to pray and to keep asking.
questions: Why does Jesus follow the Our Father with a story about persistence?
What does calling God "Father" mean to you?
What are you asking God for right now?

discuss: Which line of the Our Father do you pray most sincerely?
What does it mean to pray "thy will be done"?
How has your prayer changed since you started RCIA?

verse.text: He is not here, for he is risen, as he said. Come, and see the place where the Lord was laid.

bible.intro: Easter morning and Mary Magdalene.
questions: Mary doesn't recognize Jesus until he says her name. Why?
What do you think Jesus would say to you by name?
How do you want to spend Holy Week?

discuss: What are you most looking forward to at the Easter Vigil?
What are you nervous about?
Who will you invite to share the night with you?

verse.text: And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me.

bible.intro: Living as the early Church lived.
questions: Which of these habits do you want to keep for life?
How did the sacraments change you?
What does Sunday Mass mean to you now?

discuss: What has changed in you since Easter?
How will you stay connected to your parish?
What do you want to remember from this year?

verse.text: Going therefore, teach ye all nations; baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

bible.intro: Back to Emmaus: now you are the one who runs to tell.
questions: The disciples go back to Jerusalem the same hour. Why the hurry?
Who walked with you this year?
Who could you walk with next?

discuss: How would you tell your faith story in two minutes?
What gifts could you share with your parish?
Who is someone you could invite to Mass or RCIA next year?

challenges.title: Make the Sign of the Cross
challenges.body: Begin and end each day this week with the Sign of the Cross. Notice how it frames your day.

challenges.title: Pray the Our Father slowly
challenges.body: Once a day, pray the Our Father so slowly that you notice every word.

challenges.title: Visit a church
challenges.body: Stop into a Catholic church outside of Mass and sit quietly for five minutes.

challenges.title: Read a Gospel chapter a day
challenges.body: Start the Gospel of Mark and read one chapter each day.

challenges.title: Say grace
challenges.body: Say grace before every meal this week, even at work or in public.

challenges.title: Phone off at Mass
challenges.body: Arrive five minutes early on Sunday and leave your phone off until you're home.

challenges.title: Thank three people
challenges.body: Thank three people this week for something specific they did.

challenges.title: Fast from complaining
challenges.body: Try a day, then three, without complaining. Offer each slip-up to God.

challenges.title: Learn one prayer by heart
challenges.body: Pick one prayer from the Pray tab and practice it until you know it.

challenges.title: Pray for your sponsor
challenges.body: Pray by name for your sponsor and catechist every day.

challenges.title: A small sacrifice
challenges.body: Give up one small comfort this week and offer it for someone who is struggling.

challenges.title: Examine your day
challenges.body: Before sleep, look back on the day: where was God? Where did you fall short?

challenges.title: Ask a question
challenges.body: Bring one honest question to class or to your sponsor.

challenges.title: Write a note
challenges.body: Write a short note of encouragement to someone in your class.

challenges.title: Read about a saint
challenges.body: Read the story of the saint of the week and share one thing you learned.

challenges.title: Pray the Angelus
challenges.body: At noon, stop and pray the Angelus (or the Regina Caeli in Easter).

challenges.title: Give something away
challenges.body: Give away one thing you don't need to someone who does.

challenges.title: Forgive someone
challenges.body: Bring someone you struggle to forgive to God in prayer each day.

challenges.title: Visit the Blessed Sacrament
challenges.body: Spend fifteen minutes in Eucharistic adoration if your parish has it.

challenges.title: Read Sunday's readings early
challenges.body: Read this Sunday's readings before Mass and choose a line to listen for.

challenges.title: Pray a decade of the Rosary
challenges.body: Pray one decade of the Rosary each day this week.

challenges.title: Serve without being seen
challenges.body: Do a kind act no one will know about.

challenges.title: Call someone lonely
challenges.body: Call or visit someone who might be lonely.

challenges.title: Bless your home
challenges.body: Hang a crucifix or put a holy image somewhere you'll see it every day.

challenges.title: Pray for the dead
challenges.body: Pray Eternal Rest for someone who has died.

challenges.title: Learn a Mass response
challenges.body: Learn one Mass response by heart, like the Gloria or the Holy, Holy.

challenges.title: Unplug for an hour
challenges.body: Take one hour this week with no screens, and spend part of it in prayer.

challenges.title: Practice patience
challenges.body: Pick one situation that makes you impatient and offer it up each time.

challenges.title: Tell your story
challenges.body: Tell someone why you started RCIA.

challenges.title: Make a gratitude list
challenges.body: Write down ten things you're grateful to God for.

challenges.title: Pray for your enemies
challenges.body: Pray for someone who has hurt you, as Jesus asks (Matthew 5:44).

challenges.title: Invite someone
challenges.body: Invite a friend to Mass or to a parish event.

saintActions.augustine: Write down one thing you are still searching for, and give it to God in prayer.
saintActions.monica: Pray every day this week for someone you love who is far from God.
saintActions.mary-magdalene: Tell one person something good Jesus has done for you.
saintActions.peter: Think of a time you failed. Tell Jesus you love him anyway, as Peter did.
saintActions.paul: Write a short letter of encouragement to a friend.
saintActions.edith-stein: Spend ten minutes in silence, searching for the truth with an open heart.
saintActions.elizabeth-seton: Help a child learn something new, or pray for teachers.
saintActions.bakhita: Pray for victims of human trafficking, and forgive someone who hurt you.
saintActions.kateri: Pray outside in creation for a few minutes each day.
saintActions.therese: Do one small, hidden act of love each day, the "little way."
saintActions.francis: Give away something you don't need, and thank God for creation.
saintActions.teresa-calcutta: Do something kind for a person others overlook.
saintActions.joseph: Do your daily work carefully and quietly, offering it to God.
saintActions.john-paul-ii: Pray for young people and for your country's leaders.
saintActions.aquinas: Ask God for understanding before you read or study.
saintActions.frassati: Invite a friend on a walk or hike and pray along the way.
saintActions.carlo-acutis: Spend a few minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, or use your phone for something holy.
saintActions.gianna: Pray for mothers, doctors, and families expecting a baby.
saintActions.luke: Read a chapter of Luke's Gospel.
saintActions.cecilia: Sing or listen to a hymn as a prayer.
saintActions.kolbe: Offer a small sacrifice for someone in a hard situation.
saintActions.frances-cabrini: Welcome a newcomer, or pray for immigrants and refugees.

lectio.intro: Lectio Divina ("divine reading") is an old, simple way to pray with Scripture. Take this Sunday's Gospel and give it 15 to 20 quiet minutes, in four steps.

steps.name: Read
steps.how: Read the Gospel slowly, twice. Notice which word or phrase catches your attention.
steps.prompt: The word or phrase that stood out to me

steps.name: Reflect
steps.how: Read it again. Ask: why this word? What might God be saying to me through it today?
steps.prompt: What it might mean for my life

steps.name: Respond
steps.how: Talk to God about it, honestly, in your own words: thanks, sorrow, a request.

steps.name: Rest
steps.how: Be quiet with God for a few minutes. No words needed. Then choose one small way to live the Gospel this week.
steps.prompt: One thing I will do this week

firstConfession.intro: Your first Confession is a gift, not an exam. These steps help you prepare calmly. Nothing you tick here is saved: it disappears when you leave this page.
before: Pray to the Holy Spirit to help you see your life honestly and kindly.
Go through the questions below slowly. Tick anything you want to remember to confess.
Remember the father in the parable of the prodigal son: he runs to meet his child.
say: Make the Sign of the Cross and say: "Bless me, Father, for I have sinned. This is my first Confession."
Tell the priest your sins, simply. You can say "I'm nervous, please help me." Priests are glad to.
Listen to his advice and the penance he gives you.
Listen as he gives absolution, and answer "Amen."
after: Thank God. You are forgiven and free.
Many people say they feel lighter. Some feel nothing special, and that is fine too: the grace is real either way.
